rv.q: WHITE ROOSTER is an ambitious production fully embracing its strangeness while remaining rooted in themes of grief, love, and self-determination.
Pruning and sharpening should most certainly continue on “White Rooster,” but this type of ambitious artistic endeavor deserves all sorts of encouragement no matter how messy its current state.
White Rooster summons a realm of folklore and restless spirits in a spellbound theatrical storm.
The show defies categorization and is one of those things you just drag your friends to see.
This is a gripping and ferociously entertaining evening at the theatre, and an experience that’s as sui generis as you’re likely to get on stage.
Mr. Yee’s play is an original, incredibly inventive saga that weaves together ghosts, puppets, movement and music.
The world Yee creates is weirdly compelling and wildly funny when you get used to the dark.
However, the storyline feels underdeveloped, leaving certain plot points and character arcs unclear.
The problem, at least for this critic, is that despite the emphasis on spectacle, the show isn’t so much playful as morbidly silly, like a Halloween prank that just won’t end.
This is Lookingglass doing what it does best- creating something that may not make sense at first, but will be something that will evoke thoughts that might have never entered your mind.
Everything about White Rooster is perfectly orchestrated so that nothing feels out of place and it works together seamlessly.

cn.t: Critics praise this inventive genre-blending ghost story for its striking visual spectacle, seamless integration of puppetry, music and movement, though some find the narrative unclear and lacking depth beneath its theatrical flair.
